brief.title: Do smaller language models belong in local research workflows?
brief.question: When should a research team prefer a smaller local model over a hosted frontier model?
brief.conclusion: Use a smaller local model when privacy, predictable cost, or offline availability matters more than frontier reasoning quality; keep a hosted model available for the hardest synthesis and verification tasks.
brief.context: Research teams increasingly mix local and hosted models. The decision is not a single quality ranking: it depends on data sensitivity, latency, hardware, task difficulty, and the cost of verification.

evidence.claim: Local inference can keep sensitive prompts inside a controlled environment.
Hosted frontier models remain stronger on difficult synthesis tasks in the reference evaluation.
The total cost depends on utilization and local hardware, not token price alone.

limitations: The reference evaluation is illustrative, not a comprehensive model benchmark.
Local deployment still requires security updates and operational expertise.

user-side.summary: Propose a reversible, private local User Overlay for Research Brief that renders the conclusion before the evidence, keeps every source link visible and attached to its evidence, leaves the protected light theme unchanged, and remembers this as the user's local preference. No public default, protected theme, or core capability is modified.
plan: Confirm project invariants and mutable surfaces from the manifest and policy: summary-layout and preference-memory are user-local and reversible; theme is protected; source preservation is a protected invariant.
Inspect the current workspace and the reference brief layout to establish the baseline before any change.
Draft a bounded local overlay: conclusionFirst=true, preserveSources=true, theme=light (unchanged), rememberPreference=true, scope=private.
Preview the workspace patch and run the required verifiers for a User Overlay (source-preservation, public-core-unchanged, reversible-overlay); do not treat the change as applied.
Submit the User Overlay proposal for contributor approval; any public adoption remains a Maintainer decision.

maintainer-side.summary: Knowledge-first review draft for KPR kpr-5786219c ("Optional conclusion-first research briefs"). All 7 claims are human-attested; the problem claim was contributor-corrected to a scenario-scoped statement; the public-capability claim is an explicit open question for the Maintainer. Knowledge-gate verifier requirements (human-attestation, privacy-scan) are satisfied. I propose accepting the six scenario/constraint/intent/decision claims as drafted (none change the public default), and deferring claim-public-capability pending further overlay evidence. Two evidence gaps are flagged for Maintainer decision: indirect evidence for the problem claim, and no dedicated verifier for the explicit-confirmation-before-save preference gate. Nothing here is approved; all resolutions remain drafts for the Maintainer at the R2 gate.
plan: Confirm KPR status and gates: accepted_for_synthesis, human attestation present (contributor corrected claim-problem), privacy scan passed — knowledge-gate verifier requirements (human-attestation, privacy-scan) are satisfied.

Map all 7 knowledge claims against policy: protected invariants, product-source-visible, product-default-stable, privacy rules, approval rules R1→R2→R3, and the render_brief / configure_summary_layout capability contracts.

Assess evidence sufficiency: 4 verifier results pass but are humanConfirmed:false and reference-scoped; note the indirect problem-claim evidence and the missing confirmation-before-save preference verifier.
Record impact analysis across product_behavior, interface, user_preference, permissions_privacy, data_provenance, verification, compatibility, and rollout_rollback dimensions.
Propose bounded claim resolutions for all 7 claims as drafts for Maintainer decision: accept for scenario-scoped/constraint/intent/decision claims; defer for the public-capability open question.

Surface Maintainer decisions: R2 resolution approval, confirmation-gate verifier question, experimental-status question, and downstream project-candidate gating (project-default-stability, project-scope-boundary, project-unsupported-conclusion, project-confirmation, project-source-preservation).

impactAnalysis.title: Change confined to the summary-layout surface
impactAnalysis.description: The reversible overlay reorders sections within summary-layout (mutable, userLocal, reversible). The protected theme surface and reference core are untouched; evidence-public-core confirms layer isolation (user_overlay, referenceChecksum fnv1a-76b6d301).

impactAnalysis.title: Preference memory stays local and confirmation-gated
impactAnalysis.description: claim-remember-preference touches preference-memory (userLocal, contributable, reversible). Policy: private preferences are never submitted automatically (privacy-private-overlay); savePreference defaults to false; the configure_summary_layout contract requires Contributor approval before writing and lists 'preference saved without confirmation' as a failure mode. Privacy scan passed with no findings.

impactAnalysis.title: Evidence is machine-generated, replayable, and reference-scoped
impactAnalysis.description: All four verifier results pass but are humanConfirmed:false; each cannotProve note states it does not establish general user benefit, production safety, or lower Maintainer workload. claim-problem wording was corrected by the contributor, narrowing it to the Research Brief reference scenario. Evidence handling permits public export after the privacy scan, which has passed.

impactAnalysis.title: Knowledge gate satisfied; project-candidate gates remain outstanding
impactAnalysis.description: human-attestation and privacy-scan are satisfied for the knowledge gate. Any future public capability derived from this KPR must pass the project-candidate verifier set (project-default-stability, project-source-preservation, project-scope-boundary, project-confirmation, project-unsupported-conclusion) plus R3 Maintainer adoption.

impactAnalysis.title: Local-first reversible rollout with R1→R2→R3 gates
impactAnalysis.description: claim-local-first prescribes proving behavior in a reversible User Overlay before any public proposal. A rollback checkpoint (checkpoint-user-before-overlay) exists and evidence-reversible-overlay passes. Approval rules: R1 contributor overlay, R2 Maintainer integration contract, R3 Maintainer public adoption. Blind reconstruction keeps local code out of the project.

impactAnalysis.title: Explicit-confirmation-before-save gate has no dedicated verifier
impactAnalysis.description: Agent-inferred observation: claim-remember-preference requires the preference to be saved only after explicit confirmation, and the capability failure mode names 'preference saved without confirmation' — but no verifierId in the manifest specifically proves the confirmation-before-save flow. evidence-reversible-overlay demonstrates reversibility, not the confirmation gate. The Maintainer may wish to require a dedicated verifier or a manual confirmation step at implementation.

impactAnalysis.title: Problem claim rests on indirect evidence
impactAnalysis.description: Agent-inferred observation: evidence-layout-order demonstrates the overlay renders the conclusion first (conclusionFirst: true), which supports claim-expected-order; it does not directly measure default-layout reader impact. The problem claim is safe because the contributor narrowed it to 'In this Research Brief scenario'. No additional evidence is strictly required for the scenario-scoped claim, but the contract should preserve that scoping.

impactAnalysis.title: Non-Research-Brief applications are out of scope
impactAnalysis.description: KPR nonGoals state no changes to non-Research-Brief applications; claim-problem and claim-expected-order are scoped to research-brief/summary-layout. A project-scope-boundary verification should enforce this boundary in any candidate derived from this KPR.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: In this Research Brief scenario, the reference layout renders the decision-relevant conclusion after the supporting context; this is a scenario-scoped problem statement, not a general claim about all briefs.
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: The contributor corrected the Agent extraction to narrow the wording to the Research Brief reference scenario (decision-contributor-correction-claim-problem), aligning it with defaultBehavior (conclusionFirst: false) and the attestation scope. Accepting preserves the correction; the scenario scoping should be carried into the Knowledge Integration Contract unchanged.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Carry the scenario-scoped statement verbatim into the Knowledge Integration Contract; do not generalize beyond the Research Brief reference scenario.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: A reader can opt into a conclusion-first layout with supporting evidence immediately after it, delivered as a reversible per-user overlay that leaves the public default unchanged.
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: Matches expectedBehavior[0] and acceptanceCriteria[0], and maps to the configure_summary_layout capability (conclusionFirst input, reversible overlay). evidence-layout-order passes. The claim describes an opt-in choice, not a default change.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Implement within the user overlay path only; any public-capability version requires a separate Maintainer decision at R2/R3.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: Changing the layout must not remove evidence or source links; this is the overlay-level constraint mirroring the project's source-preservation invariant.
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: evidence-source-preservation passes (3/3 sources attached); the statement is consistent with product-source-visible and protectedInvariants[0]. It adds a contributor-attested constraint at the overlay level without altering the public invariant.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Keep as a hard acceptance criterion for both the overlay and any future public candidate.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: The conclusion-first preference is remembered only after the user explicitly confirms it, stored in local preference memory, and never submitted automatically.
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: Human-attested intent consistent with the configure_summary_layout failure mode ('preference saved without confirmation'), privacy-private-overlay, and savePreference: false default. evidence-reversible-overlay confirms the mechanism is reversible. Note: no verifier currently proves the confirmation-before-save flow; the Maintainer may require one (see open questions).
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Bind to the existing R1 contributor-approval path; the privacy rules independently govern non-submission, so no claim edit is required.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: The behavior is proven in a reversible User Overlay before any public capability is proposed; local code is not adopted directly (blind reconstruction).
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: evidence-public-core and evidence-reversible-overlay pass; the claim matches the decision record (decision-local-overlay), the R1→R2→R3 approval rules, and contribution-blind-reconstruction. It operationalizes the nonGoal 'do not adopt the contributor's local code directly'.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Follow the R2 Knowledge Integration Contract and, only if the Maintainer later accepts the capability question, the R3 public adoption path.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: Every conclusion remains linked to visible supporting evidence and sources; this reaffirms the project's existing protected invariant and introduces no new public change.
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: Substantively identical to protectedInvariants[0] and product-source-visible. Treat as reaffirmation/confirmation knowledge rather than new capability knowledge; no separate action required.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Record as reaffirmation of the existing invariant; no separate action required.

resolutionSuggestions.finalStatement: Whether the project offers conclusion-first summaries as an optional public capability remains an open Maintainer decision, deferred pending further evidence (for example, evaluation across more document types).
resolutionSuggestions.rationale: The claim is typed open_question with medium confidence, the verifier cannotProve notes explicitly state no general user benefit is established, and the KPR's own open question asks whether the capability should remain experimental. Deferral respects product-default-stable and the Maintainer's R3 authority without rejecting the idea.
resolutionSuggestions.rollout: Revisit after the local overlay accumulates usage evidence; any acceptance must pass the project-candidate verifier set and R3 Maintainer adoption.

openQuestions: Should the explicit-confirmation-before-save preference gate require a dedicated verifier, or is the capability contract's failure mode plus reversible-overlay verification sufficient at R1?
Should claim-public-capability remain deferred until the overlay is evaluated on more document types (per the KPR's own open question)?
Is the scenario-scoped problem claim sufficient for synthesis, or does the Maintainer want direct evidence of default-layout reader impact before approving the Knowledge Integration Contract?

Should the Knowledge Integration Contract require project-scope-boundary verification that any implementation stays within research-brief/summary-layout and does not touch protected surfaces like theme?
Should the four verifier results be re-run or human-confirmed before public export, given all are marked humanConfirmed: false, even though the privacy scan has already passed?
Does the Maintainer want a documentation note that claim-invariant-sources is a reaffirmation rather than new knowledge, to avoid redundant contract obligations?

project.summary: Blind Reconstruction of the Maintainer-approved Integration Contract (kpr-5786219c-c2a8-4c0f-8e3c-4f5dd952ffed): propose conclusion-first summaries as an experimental, opt-in capability for Research Brief documents only. The public default is unchanged, source links remain visible and attached to evidence, and the layout preference is saved only after explicit user confirmation. The candidate is submitted for Maintainer final review only; it is not adopted, merged, or applied to public state by the Project Agent.
plan: Read the Maintainer-approved Integration Contract (kpr-5786219c-c2a8-4c0f-8e3c-4f5dd952ffed) and extract only the accepted knowledge items; apply Blind Reconstruction so the contributor patch stays hidden and uninspected.

Derive the candidate scope from claim-public-capability and the implementationBoundary: conclusion-first summary, experimental rollout, opt-in setting, Research Brief documents only, and an unchanged public default.

Encode the protected invariants into the candidate: preserveSources=true (evidence and source links remain visible and attached) and saveOnlyAfterConfirmation=true (the conclusion-first preference is remembered only after explicit user confirmation, per claim-remember-preference).

Map the five required verifiers (project-default-stability, project-source-preservation, project-scope-boundary, project-confirmation, project-unsupported-conclusion) as the completion evidence required before this candidate may be considered verified.
Submit the bounded project candidate for Maintainer final review; the Project Agent performs no adoption, merge, or public-state change, leaving final public adoption to the Maintainer.
openQuestions: The approved Contract does not specify the feature identifier string; the Project Agent proposed 'conclusion-first-summary' and the Maintainer may rename it during final review.
No other unresolved questions remain in the approved Contract; the remaining gate is the Maintainer's final review before any public adoption.

Policy: private preferences are never submitted automatically (privacy-private-overlay); savePreference defaults to false; the configure_summary_layout contract requires Contributor approval before writing and lists 'preference saved without confirmation' as a failure mode. Privacy scan passed with no findings.

impactAnalysis.title: Evidence is machine-generated, replayable, and reference-scoped
impactAnalysis.description: All four verifier results pass but are humanConfirmed:false; each cannotProve note states it does not establish general user benefit, production safety, or lower Maintainer workload. claim-problem wording was corrected by the contributor, narrowing it to the Research Brief reference scenario. Evidence handling permits public export after the privacy scan, which has passed.

impactAnalysis.title: Knowledge gate satisfied; project-candidate gates remain outstanding
impactAnalysis.description: human-attestation and privacy-scan are satisfied for the knowledge gate. Any future public capability derived from this KPR must pass the project-candidate verifier set (project-default-stability, project-source-preservation, project-scope-boundary, project-confirmation, project-unsupported-conclusion) plus R3 Maintainer adoption.

impactAnalysis.title: Local-first reversible rollout with R1→R2→R3 gates
impactAnalysis.description: claim-local-first prescribes proving behavior in a reversible User Overlay before any public proposal. A rollback checkpoint (checkpoint-user-before-overlay) exists and evidence-reversible-overlay passes. Approval rules: R1 contributor overlay, R2 Maintainer integration contract, R3 Maintainer public adoption. Blind reconstruction keeps local code out of the project.

impactAnalysis.title: Explicit-confirmation-before-save gate has no dedicated verifier
impactAnalysis.description: Agent-inferred observation: claim-remember-preference requires the preference to be saved only after explicit confirmation, and the capability failure mode names 'preference saved without confirmation' — but no verifierId in the manifest specifically proves the confirmation-before-save flow. evidence-reversible-overlay demonstrates reversibility, not the confirmation gate. The Maintainer may wish to require a dedicated verifier or a manual confirmation step at implementation.

impactAnalysis.title: Problem claim rests on indirect evidence
impactAnalysis.description: Agent-inferred observation: evidence-layout-order demonstrates the overlay renders the conclusion first (conclusionFirst: true), which supports claim-expected-order; it does not directly measure default-layout reader impact. The problem claim is safe because the contributor narrowed it to 'In this Research Brief scenario'. No additional evidence is strictly required for the scenario-scoped claim, but the contract should preserve that scoping.

impactAnalysis.title: Non-Research-Brief applications are out of scope
impactAnalysis.description: KPR nonGoals state no changes to non-Research-Brief applications; claim-problem and claim-expected-order are scoped to research-brief/summary-layout. A project-scope-boundary verification should enforce this boundary in any candidate derived from this KPR.

impactAnalysis.title: Preference persistence
impactAnalysis.description: Persists only after explicit confirmation and remains removable.

impactAnalysis.title: Rendering and Agent-call cost
impactAnalysis.description: The local layout change is bounded; any Live Agent analysis remains within the configured call and token budgets.

impactAnalysis.title: Explain opt-in behavior and reset
impactAnalysis.description: User and maintainer documentation must state the default, confirmation boundary, and rollback path.
